_source: AI-researched NEW DISTRICT candidates for Manchester and Cheshire, awaiting review — never directly promoted by the research agent. Populated by the same daily scheduled research agent as venue-suggestions.json (2026-08, at explicit user request), committed straight to master the same way (see that file's own doc comment for why). Expected to be rare: the research brief (.claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md) treats district suggestions as an occasional finding (a genuinely distinct, not-yet-covered high-end area within Manchester or Cheshire), not a daily quota — most days should add zero entries here. The daily curia-suggestion-review agent (.claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md) is the only thing that promotes an entry into the real docs/data/districts.json, behind its own pull request. Each entry mirrors docs/data/districts.json's own raw shape (name/metro/lat/lon/base/kind/accentColor/editorialDescription) so an approved entry can be copied straight in, plus review-only fields (suggestedDate, status, researchNotes) stripped on promotion. `metro` must be 'manchester' or 'cheshire' only — never 'los-angeles' or a new metro (out of scope, per the user's explicit 'shouldn't go beyond cheshire and manchester just yet').
_reviewWorkflow: Same as venue-suggestions.json: status starts 'pending', the review agent flips it to 'approved' (then copies fields into districts.json, as part of its own PR) or 'rejected' (kept here with researchNotes so it isn't re-suggested). A human's real review happens by reading/merging that PR.

suggestions.name: Rusholme (Curry Mile)
suggestions.editorialDescription: Wilmslow Road doesn't quieten until well past midnight, and the queue outside the good dessert parlours is the real tell that nothing here is coasting on the old name. What began as a strip of curry houses has widened into Yemeni grills, Persian rice cellars and family kitchens three decades deep — walk past the ends where the chains cluster and the best of it still sits mid-strip, unbothered by fashion or footfall counts.
suggestions.researchNotes: Found via this run's required per-day new-district check, not user-named. Rusholme's 'Curry Mile' (the stretch of Wilmslow Road roughly between Anson Road and Dickenson Road) is one of the most nationally recognisable food destinations in the country and squarely passes the 'a local would raise an eyebrow this isn't already covered' test — no existing Manchester-metro district (the nearest, Chorlton and Chinatown, are genuinely different strips with different characters) covers it. Verified via visitmanchester.com's own dedicated Curry Mile guide, manchestertourism.org, Tripadvisor and current 2026 restaurant coverage: over 70 restaurants, shisha cafes and sweet shops line the road; the scene has genuinely diversified past its original curry-house identity into Yemeni grills, Palestinian bakeries, Persian rice specialists, shisha lounges and dessert parlours with real queues past 11pm — a distinct, still-evolving identity, not a fossilised tourist strip. Coordinates (53.455814, -2.225671) are the M14 5TQ postcode centroid on Wilmslow Road itself (doogal.co.uk), independently verified rather than invented, and land well within the existing lat 53.0-53.6/lon -2.6--2.0 sanity box. Distance check: roughly 2.5 miles south of the city centre and comfortably distinct from Chorlton (Curia's nearest existing district, ~2 miles further south-west) and Chinatown (~2 miles north) — no overlap. accentColor (#B8542E, a muted paprika/burnt-orange evoking the spice and neon of the strip) chosen for perceptual distinctness against the district accents it would actually render alongside at city zoom (Chorlton's sage green #6B8F71, Didsbury's dusty rose #B98098, Northern Quarter's plum #8B6FA8, Chinatown's crimson-berry #A73F52, Ancoats' rust-brick #9C5030, Deansgate's orange #D68A3F, Spinningfields' soft blue #6E8FA6) — distinct from all of them, including its closest hue-neighbour Chester's sandstone-red (#A6512F), which never renders alongside it given the real distance between the two. base (74) is a reasoned estimate, similar register to Chorlton (78) and above Chinatown (68) — a genuinely high-footfall, late-running strip, not a quiet one. kind 'city', matching every other Manchester-metro district. No district group added — Rusholme doesn't fit any existing group's real geography (the Deansgate Spine and Ancoats & the NQ groups are both inner-city-core, a different cluster). No venues suggested for it in this same run — same 'district entry only, venues as separate follow-up work' precedent every prior district promotion has followed; candidates worth a future pass once this district exists include independent, non-chain kitchens found during this same research session (e.g. Bardez, Mughli Charcoal Pit) — neither verified to Curia's full Hard rule 1 bar here, since a venue can't be suggested against a district id that doesn't exist yet.

suggestions.name: Monton
suggestions.editorialDescription: A Salford village that decided against the chain-pub wave entirely — Monton Road's quarter-mile doing more independent cafés, wine shops and small kitchens per yard than anywhere else in the conurbation, with the Bridgewater Canal a two-minute walk from whichever one you pick.
suggestions.researchNotes: Found via this run's required per-day new-district check, not user-named. Monton is a genuinely distinct, well-known Salford village consistently described in Greater Manchester food/drink coverage as a 'dining village' — confirmed via confidentials.com ('An insider's guide to eating and drinking in Monton'), manchestersfinest.com and ilovemanchester.com ('Monton is a colourful day and night destination filled with buzzing independents'), all explicitly describing a roughly 0.4-mile stretch of Monton Road/Eccles Old Road as unusually independent-dense (cafés-turned-wine-bars, bistros, delis, natural-wine shops, a canalside pub) rather than chain-anchored. Passes this run's own 'would a local raise an eyebrow this isn't already covered' test the same way Prestbury/Knutsford/Cheadle Hulme originally did. Distinct from every existing Manchester-metro district: nearest are Chorlton (~8.5km SE) and Northern Quarter (~8km E), both well past this file's own established close-adjacent-district precedent (Heaton Moor/Stockport Underbanks, a few hundred metres apart; Bramhall/Cheadle Hulme, ~2 miles) — a clean gap, not a marginal case. Coordinates (53.485/-2.356) derived from Monton's OS grid reference (SJ767994, per Wikipedia) cross-checked against nearby M30-postcode geocodes found during this search (53.484-53.486/-2.339 to -2.356) — lands on Monton Road itself; doogal.co.uk/api.postcodes.io were both blocked by the network egress proxy this session, so this is a triangulated estimate rather than a direct geocode, flagged for the reviewer to tighten. Metro assigned 'manchester' as Greater Manchester shorthand, the same judgment already applied to Stockport (Underbanks)/Heaton Moor/Cheadle Hulme/Bramhall (Salford is one of Greater Manchester's ten metropolitan boroughs). kind 'city' — a dense, walkable high street, not a rural county town. accentColor (#5E7A7D, a muted canal-teal nodding to the Bridgewater Canal running along the village) checked for perceptual distinctness against every existing accent, closest neighbours Northwich's river-slate teal (#4A6B6E) and Heaton Moor's dusty blue-grey (#6B7F94) — distinct from both, and neither ever renders alongside Monton given the real distance involved. base (70) is a reasoned estimate, similar register to Chorlton's own starting point (78) given a comparable 'independent-density' identity at a slightly smaller scale. No district group added — Monton doesn't fit any existing group's real geography. No venues suggested for it in this same run — same 'district entry only, venues as separate follow-up work' precedent every prior district promotion has followed; one operator found during this research (The Makers Market, which runs a monthly market at nearby West Didsbury and elsewhere across the North West/Midlands) was deliberately not suggested as a venue anywhere — a genuine multi-town recurring-event footprint that reads closer to a chain than a single-site venue, and Hard rule 1's own guidance is to drop a candidate when genuinely unsure rather than include it.
